children: Shares of oil and gas company Granite Ridge Resources
fell 5.7% in the afternoon session after crude oil prices tumbled as renewed diplomatic talks between the United States and Iran eased concerns over potential Middle East supply disruptions.

Brent crude fell by more than 4%, while broader crude benchmarks dropped 3% following reports that negotiators convened in Doha to develop a framework for an agreement. For energy producers, crude prices directly dictate top-line revenue and operating margins. When geopolitical tensions flare across vital oil-producing regions, markets build in a risk premium, which is an additional cost priced into commodities to compensate for potential disruption risks.

Progress in diplomatic dialogue deflates this geopolitical risk premium, pushing oil prices lower. As the threat of imminent disruption to global supply routes recedes, investors quickly recalibrate expected cash flows for exploration and production firms, leading to widespread declines across the energy industry.
What is the market telling us

Granite Ridge Resources’s shares are quite volatile and have had 16 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 25 days ago when the stock gained 3.6% on the news that a Gulf tanker attack slowed traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, while hurricane-driven production halts shut in Gulf of Mexico output, the Financial Times noted. The resulting supply squeeze lifted Brent crude above $104 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate to $92, according to CNBC. When global supplies face sudden restrictions, benchmark crude prices tend to spike, boosting revenue expectations and profitability for major oil and gas producers across the energy industry.

Granite Ridge Resources is up 14.3% since the beginning of the year, but at $5.35 per share, it is still trading 12.5% below its 52-week high of $6.11 from May 2026. Despite the year-to-date gain, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Granite Ridge Resources’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $543.05.
